comments.content: The batched update functions use `Promise.all` with `context.globalState.update` and `storeSecret`. VS Code's `globalState.update` and `secrets.store` are already asynchronous but may not benefit from parallelization since they likely serialize internally. Consider measuring if this actually improves performance vs sequential updates, or if it adds overhead. Also, `updateSecretsBatch` passes `value` directly to `storeSecret` which expects `value?: string` - this is correct since `Record<string, string | undefined>` matches.

The batched updates include all keys unconditionally. If some values are `undefined`, they will be written as `undefined` to global state, which may differ from the previous behavior where `updateGlobalState` might have been skipped for undefined values. Check if `updateGlobalState` handles `undefined` by deleting the key or storing it. If the previous code only called `updateGlobalState` when values were defined, this change could introduce unintended keys with `undefined` values.

Added performance logging with `console.log` statements. These will appear in the developer console for all users. Consider using a debug-only logging mechanism (e.g., checking `process.env.NODE_ENV` or a feature flag) so these don't ship to production, or at least use a namespaced logger that can be disabled.

Frontend performance logging added. Same concern as backend - `console.log` statements will be visible to all users in browser devtools. Consider wrapping in a debug flag or using a proper logging utility that respects log levels.
